In Table 1: For General subset, offline Filtered BC success 51.7% vs DigiRL 63.5; improvement in offline ~11.8% absolute. For online, Filtered BC 61.5% vs Digi RL 71.9% improvement ~10.4%. For Web Shopping: offline Filtered BC 44.7% vs DigiRL 62.8% difference 18.1%. Online: Filtered BC 57.8% vs DigiRL 67.2% diff 9.4%. So statement about Web Shopping 3.6% doesn't match; that's not correct. There's also no mention of 3.6% anywhere. So statement A is false.

b. "The all possible actions for the agent in the DigiRL framework include tapping and swiping on the screen using normalized coordinates and typing variable-level text inputs." This matches description: Agent receives screenshot; action space includes tapping and sliding based on normalized (x,y) coordinates (range 1 to 1). It also includes typing text strings of variable length. Also pressing cursor etc. So statement b is correct. But need to check but nuance: "swiping on the screen using normalized coordinates". In action space: "tapping and sliding based on normalized (x,y) coordinates (ranging from 0 to 1 relative to the screen dimensions)" which includes sliding and tapping; yes.

"The automatic curriculum in DigiRL adjusts the Instruction-level value function to filter out of easy tasks, allowing the agent to focus solely on tasks it has not yet encountered during training." The explanation: Instruction-level value function is used to prioritize tasks that contribute high learning signal; for tasks with highest A_instruct, that indicates a difficult task (the agent succeeded but value small). So the curriculum directs to sample tasks with high A_instruct. It doesn't filter out easy tasks because it selects hard steps. The statement says "filter out easy tasks, allowing the agent to focus solely on tasks it has not yet encountered during training." Actually the curriculum samples tasks and maybe discards tasks with high success. It's a bit misled: instead of only certain tasks that do not appear might be correct. But the phrase says "allow the agent to focus solely on tasks it has not yet encountered during training." The curriculum uses the value function to select tasks with high value to assist learning. Not necessarily focusing only on unseen tasks. Also "filter out easy tasks" indicates selecting hard tasks. So statement might partially correct? But maybe the statement refers to "actively filter out easy tasks". Option A & D but we see only B is correct.

d. "The cross-entropy loss function is applied in Digi RL exclusively to the policy network, avoiding its use in the training of value functions to prevent overfitting in the model." This mentions cross-entropy used only for parameters of policy. But text: "Implementation details... we utilize a cross-entropy objective based on the Monte-Carlo estimate of the trajectory reward for practice both. L(V_traj). L(V_step).
